name: Pre-Socratic
description: The dawn of Western philosophy: transition from mythos to logos, cosmological inquiries into the arche (first principle) of all things.

name: Classical Greek
description: Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle: systematic exploration of ethics, epistemology, politics, metaphysics, and logic.

name: Hellenistic & Roman
description: Philosophy as an art of living (the therapeutic turn): Stoics, Epicureans, Skeptics, and Neoplatonists seeking tranquility and virtue.

name: Eastern & Axial Traditions
description: Foundational Asian philosophical inquiry: Daoism, Confucianism, Early Buddhism, Nagarjuna, and Advaita Vedanta.

name: Medieval & Islamic Golden Age
description: Synthesis of classical philosophy with Abrahamic theology: Scholasticism, Avicenna, Averroes, Aquinas, and Ockham.

name: Early Modern & Scientific
description: Epistemological turn, breakdown of scholasticism, Cartesian doubt, Continental Rationalism, and British Empiricism.

name: Enlightenment & Social Contract
description: Reason, liberty, political contracts, skepticism toward dogma: Locke, Hume, Voltaire, Rousseau, and Adam Smith.

name: German Idealism & Romanticism
description: Kant's Copernican revolution in philosophy, reconciling rationalism and empiricism; Hegel's dialectical historical spirit.

name: 19th Century Divergences
description: Revaluations, will, alienation, and radical critique: Schopenhauer, Kierkegaard, Marx, Nietzsche, and Utilitarianism.

name: 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis
description: Divergence of Analytic philosophy (logic, language games) and Continental traditions (phenomenology, existentialism, critical theory).

name: Contemporary & Post-Structural
description: Power, deconstruction, ethics in the technological age, burnout culture, simulation, and justice.
